summary: The FCC proposal to sunset E-Rate would have significant negative impacts on schools, as the FCC's proposal points to the progress schools have made in expanding broadband connectivity over the past three decades. But the fact that schools are connected today is, in large part, evidence of the success of E-Rate — not evidence that the need for the program has disappeared. Connectivity must be maintained, upgraded, secured, and maintained The school district emphasizes the critical role of E-Rate funding in maintaining and securing network infrastructure, arguing that reducing or eliminating the program would have significant budgetary and operational impacts. The district urges the FCC to preserve and improve the program rather than sunset it. The text urges the Commission to protect E-Rate and not reduce its role.
